meta.title: ytmGO — a native YouTube Music app for your desktop
meta.description: ytmGO is a free, open-source YouTube Music desktop client for macOS, Windows and Linux that brings Spotify's desktop design language to YouTube Music, with synced lyrics, on-demand video and an encrypted account session that never leaves your device.
nav.label: Main
hero.eyebrow: Free and open source · macOS · Windows · Linux
hero.title: Your music deserves more than a browser tab
hero.lead: YouTube Music has no official desktop app on macOS, Windows or Linux. ytmGO brings Spotify's desktop design language to the YouTube Music catalogue, with lyrics that keep time, video when you want it, and a library that's there the moment you open the app.
hero.note: Apache-2.0 · No account needed to start listening
shot.home: The ytmGO home screen: the library sidebar, quick picks, a Listen again shelf and the player bar.

lyrics.title: Lyrics that keep time
lyrics.body: The current line lights up and stays centred as the song plays. Scroll to read ahead whenever you like; one click on “Follow playback” brings you back to the beat.
lyrics.tick1: Drag through the lyrics and let go to jump to that line
lyrics.tick2: Opens to the lyrics the first time you press play
lyrics.tick3: Make room for the words by shrinking the cover
lyrics.demo: An animation of synchronized lyrics highlighting one line at a time.
library.title: Right where you left it
library.body: Your playlists, albums and artists appear the moment ytmGO opens, then refresh quietly in the background. Quit in the middle of a song, and next time it waits at the same second, paused until you press play.
library.tick1: Home, Explore, Search and Library, straight from YouTube Music
library.tick2: Keep scrolling and the next page is already loading
library.tick3: Back and Forward return to pages exactly as you left them
shot.album: An album page in ytmGO with a large cover, a play button and a numbered track list.
immersive.title: Let the music take the whole screen
immersive.body: Immersive mode puts the cover, the lyrics and the queue across the whole window. Switch from the cover to the music video at any time: it stays in step with the audio, and the moment you hide it, the decoder stops while the music plays on.
immersive.tick1: Video from 144p up to 1080p, 720p by default
immersive.tick2: Your chosen quality is kept across tracks and restarts
immersive.tick3: Hiding the video releases its decoder instantly
shot.immersive: Immersive mode: a large cover beside synchronized lyrics with the current line highlighted.
layout.title: Fits however you listen
layout.body: A full sidebar on a wide screen, a slim rail in between, and a mini player with tabs when the window is narrow. Light or dark, in four languages, and it switches without interrupting the song.
shot.light: ytmGO in light appearance with the full library sidebar.
shot.compact: ytmGO in a narrow window, with a mini player above a bottom tab bar.
speed.title: Smooth at 60fps, easy on memory
speed.body: Scroll through a playlist of 2,600+ tracks, resize from a wide desktop down to a mini player, and switch theme or language live without interrupting the music.
speed.fps.label: Scrolling 2,600+ track playlists and resizing live
speed.paused.label: Restored session, paused
speed.playing.label: Median while playing with synced lyrics
speed.note: Measured on Apple silicon across the whole process tree, every helper process included, with scripts/diagnostics/measure.py from the repository.
more.title: Thoughtful down to the details
more.keys.title: Keyboard first
more.keys.body: Search with ⌘K or Ctrl+K, control playback without the mouse, and set a global shortcut to play or pause from any app.
more.system.title: Part of your system
more.system.body: Your system's media controls, the menu bar or tray icon and the app menus all drive the same player.
more.native.title: Native, not a wrapper
more.native.body: The music window is drawn by Go, not by a bundled browser. A system web view opens only to sign in or, when needed, to verify playback.
more.updates.title: Updates itself, safely
more.updates.body: Each update is checked against an Ed25519 signature before it installs, and your account and settings carry over.
more.accounts.title: Premium or not
more.accounts.body: Listen signed out, with a free account or with YouTube Music Premium. Your membership is read from YouTube's own answer, never guessed.
more.proxy.title: Respects your network
more.proxy.body: HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY apply to every request, and on macOS ytmGO follows the system proxy settings too.
privacy.title: Your account stays yours
privacy.lead: ytmGO keeps as little as it can, encrypts what it must keep, and lets you remove all of it.
privacy.signin.title: Sign in on Google's own page
privacy.signin.body: Sign-in happens on Google's real page in a separate window that closes when you're done. There's no browser extension and no local login server.
privacy.encrypt.title: Encrypted on your device
privacy.encrypt.body: Your session is sealed with AES-256-GCM. The only thing kept in your Keychain, Credential Manager or Secret Service is its 32-byte key.
privacy.diag.title: Diagnostics stay local
privacy.diag.body: Diagnostic files record only fixed status codes: no addresses, cookies, account IDs or logs, and nothing is uploaded.
privacy.signout.title: Signing out means gone
privacy.signout.body: “Sign out and clear local data” deletes the encrypted session and its key. Your Google session in other browsers stays untouched.
download.lead: Free for macOS, Windows and Linux. Each download comes straight from the project's GitHub releases.

faq.title: Questions, answered
faq.official.q: Is ytmGO made by Google, YouTube or Spotify?
faq.official.a: No. ytmGO is an unofficial, independent open-source client. It isn't affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Google LLC, YouTube or Spotify.
faq.premium.q: Do I need YouTube Music Premium?
faq.premium.a: No. You can listen without signing in, with a free account, or with Premium. Signing in brings in your own library and likes.
faq.free.a: No. ytmGO is free and open source under the Apache License 2.0.
faq.passkey.q: Can I sign in with a passkey on macOS?
faq.passkey.a: Not at the moment. Apple only lets an app use passkeys for websites it's associated with, and an independent app can't be associated with google.com. Choose another way to verify on Google's sign-in page.
faq.smartscreen.q: Why does Windows warn me about the installer?
faq.smartscreen.a: The installer isn't Authenticode-signed yet, so SmartScreen may ask you to confirm. Updates delivered inside the app are still verified with an Ed25519 signature before they install.
faq.updates.a: ytmGO checks shortly after it starts and then once a day, and lets you install, postpone or skip each update. With Homebrew you can also run brew upgrade --cask --greedy. A Linux .deb install updates when you install the newer .deb with apt.
faq.data.q: What does ytmGO keep on my computer?
faq.data.a: Only what it needs to start where you left off: the encrypted session, a snapshot of your library, your place in the queue and your preferences. Covers that YouTube marks as public are cached for up to a day; your avatar never is.
